---
title: "UK company data: explained, connected, usable"
toc: false
---

UK company data is free, large and genuinely useful — and awkward to use. It is spread across
several registers, published in formats built for filing rather than analysis, and shaped by
rules that are easy to misread. This site does three things: it **explains** what Companies
House and the other UK sources publish, it **connects** them by showing how they join and what
each adds, and it **publishes** tested, ready-to-use datasets built from them. Where code adds
something beyond what already exists, we add it; where it doesn't, we link to the best existing
explanation instead.

This is methodology and open data, **not a company-rating product**. Register records can
support due-diligence signals; they cannot establish that a company is trustworthy, solvent or
non-fraudulent. Nothing here produces a composite score, publishes named company results, or
includes personal data.

## Start here

Pick the path that matches what you want.

- **You want data to analyse.** Start with [the accounts dataset](datasets/accounts.qmd) —
  one row per company per accounting period, 2014–2026, with a quickstart snippet and a column
  dictionary. Read [the pitfalls](guide/pitfalls.qmd) before modelling; several of them
  (dashes, restatements, mis-tagged employee counts) change results quietly if missed.
- **You want code.** The pipeline is on [GitHub](https://github.com/ThomasHSimm/open-company-uk).
  [The accounts guide](guide/accounts-data.qmd) explains the source format, and [the validation
  page](datasets/accounts-validation.qmd) explains how the extractor was checked against two
  independent parsers. The [indicator rules](indicators/methodology.qmd) are generated from
  code, so the documentation cannot drift from the implementation.
- **You want evidence.** [The landscape](landscape/who-uses.qmd) covers who uses UK company
  data and [what the commercial market charges](landscape/market.qmd). [Prior
  work](evidence/prior-work.qmd) summarises what others have built, and the [evidence
  register](evidence/register.qmd) is where sources are catalogued as they are reviewed.

## What this is, and is not

- **No composite score, anywhere.** The indicator pipeline records discrete, registrar-sourced
  facts as flags with a severity and an evidence string. Severity grades the seriousness of the
  recorded state, not confidence in it. There is no single number.
- **No named results, no personal data.** The repository publishes code, methodology and
  synthetic fixtures only. Run outputs, officer/PSC-level data and named flag lists stay
  private. The published accounts datasets contain financial facts and company numbers only.
- **Open licence.** Source data is Crown copyright, published under the Open Government Licence
  v3.0 and free to reuse with attribution. The OGL does not cover personal data, which is part
  of why personal data is removed before anything is published.

## Reading the confidence labels

Figures across this site carry one of three labels, and each carries its **source's** confidence
— the label is not an independent re-verification by this site unless it says so:

- **[Checked]** — either a **project measurement** traceable to a committed repo file (e.g.
  dataset coverage, the 99.999% parser agreement, iXBRL adoption), *or* an official/primary source
  as recorded in the repo's source material (e.g. the register statistics from the Companies House
  annual report). Where it is the latter, the label inherits that source's confidence; it has not
  been independently re-derived here. Project measurements are tagged "(project measurement)".
- **[Estimated]** — a reputable secondary source or a study estimate (e.g. the user-value figures,
  most commercial prices). Treat as indicative.
- **[Not verified]** — flagged uncertain by its own source, or not re-checked here (e.g. the FAME
  and Beauhurst prices, the API rate limit, a civil-service spend total). Confirm before relying
  on it.

Commercial prices are indicative, dated to the source, and negotiable; legislation dates (the
2025 thresholds, the 2028 reforms) are given with their confirmation date because they have moved
before.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Companies House or the Insolvency Service.
